study_identification_part.si_4_title: Dissimilarity in Sulcal Width Patterns in the Cortex can be Used to Identify Patients With Schizophrenia With Extreme Deficits in Cognitive Performance

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Normative modeling implemented using the person-based similarity index (PBSI), specifically PBSI-SW.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: The person-based similarity index (PBSI) of brain morphology indexes an individual's morphometric similarity across numerous cortical regions amongst a sample of healthy subjects. By employing a normative modeling approach on longitudinal data, we determined an individual's degree of morphometric dissimilarity to the norm.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: PBSI-SW (person-based similarity index for sulcal width).
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: We calculated the PBSI for sulcal width (PBSI-SW) in patients with schizophrenia and healthy control subjects (164 patients and 164 healthy controls; 656 magnetic resonance imaging scans) and associated it with cognitive performance and cortical sulcation index.

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: GAMMs modeled age and diagnosis with an age × diagnosis interaction, controlling for scanner and total brain volume with a random effect of the individual.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: generalized additive mixed models (GAMMs) were used. GAMM models were implemented to examine age, diagnosis (ie, patient vs control), and an age × diagnosis interaction while controlling for scanner, total brain volume, and the random effect of the individual.
